headline: Ghost Font evades AI detection with motion-based text
summary: This new font uses motion and decoys to create messages readable by humans but indecipherable to leading AI models, even when screenshotted.
details: Ghost Font is an experimental graphical communication method that uses motion, video, noise, and decoys to create text messages. While the letters are still readable to the human eye, even advanced AI models struggle to decipher them.

Unlike traditional fonts, Ghost Font's letters are composed of dots that blend with the background when static. This means a single screenshot of the message will appear as an indecipherable jumble of dots, rendering it useless for AI analysis.

Leading AI models like Claude Fable and GPT Sol 5.6 Ultra were tested with videos generated by Ghost Font. They encountered significant difficulties in decoding the moving messages, often requiring specific prompts to even attempt decipherment.

Even after extensive analysis, some AI models hallucinated incorrect messages or failed to extract the intended text. This contrasts sharply with older methods like Sang Mun's ZXX font, which modern AIs can read with ease.

To further thwart AI, Ghost Font incorporates a decoy message into each video. This serves as a final layer of obfuscation, potentially tricking AI agents into believing the decoy is the actual hidden message.

While encryption remains the ultimate method for hiding information, Ghost Font explores the possibility of creating shareable visual messages that are resistant to AI interpretation. It aims to preserve a unique human creative voice in an era of AI-driven content generation.

Potential applications for Ghost Font include enhancing CAPTCHA systems, making them more resistant to AI bots while remaining accessible to humans. It could also serve as a benchmark for evaluating the visual perception capabilities of AI models.
